question.problem: A new drug has a $64%$ probability of curing a patient within a week. If $50$ patients are treated, what is the standard deviation of the number of cured patients within a week? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.

current_example.problem: A fair five-sided die is rolled $8$ times. What is the standard deviation of the number of times we get an even number? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
current_example.worked_solution:
Let the random variable $X$ be equal to the number of times we get an even number.

Here, we have the following information:

- there are $n=8$ rolls of the die

- the probability of getting an even number (i.e., a $2,$ or $4$) on any roll of the die is

$$
p=\dfrac{2}{5} .
$$

So, $X$ follows a binomial distribution, where $X\sim B\left(8,\dfrac25\right).$

For a binomial random variable $X,$ the standard deviation is given by

$$
\textrm{SD}[X] = \sqrt{\textrm{Var}[X]}=\sqrt{np(1-p)},
$$

where $n$ is the number of experiments, and $p$ is the probability of success on each experiment.

So, the standard deviation of the number of times we get an even number is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{np(1-p)} \\  & =\sqrt{8\cdot \frac{2}{5}\cdot (1-\frac{2}{5})} \\  & =\sqrt{1.92} \\  & =1.386\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
